1. Executive Summary

Current-state audit shows that the workbook is a distributed mini-application: employee input, accounting mappings, tax logic, OLE attachments, email drafting, printing and a 24-column ERP export are combined in one macro-enabled file. The target platform will preserve the validated business outcomes while removing fragile spreadsheet formulas, desktop automation and email-based approval.

The recommended target is a vendor-neutral, self-hostable web platform with a responsive Employee Portal, Manager Approval Inbox, Finance & Accounting Cockpit, Corporate Card Reconciliation module, Admin/Master Data area, deterministic ERP Posting Engine, object-storage evidence repository and immutable audit trail.
Employee creates a report and adds up to 50 expenses one by one; photo/PDF upload is native and mobile-friendly.
OCR/document extraction proposes fields; the user confirms low-confidence data rather than retyping everything.
Manager approves or rejects in the platform; email is only a notification channel.
Finance can edit any data, but the employee-submitted revision is retained and every change is auditable.
Missing ERP vendor may proceed through approval but blocks ERP readiness until Finance resolves the Vendor Request.
VAT and FX become effective-dated master data; 5% is inactive for new expenses; car expenses use confirmed 50% deductibility.
Company-card expenses reconcile to imported bank statements; actual bank-settled RON can replace the estimate for ERP.
ERP output remains XLSX, worksheet name Import, exact current 24-column order; unused columns stay configurable for later activation.
No historical expense migration; only required master data is migrated. Legacy Excel remains archived/read-only.

Key control: ERP generation is no longer a button that can run on incomplete data. It is a gated state transition backed by preflight checks, immutable export batches and duplicate-posting prevention.

3. Excel/VBA Audit
The reverse engineering baseline remains the v5 unlocked workbook. The meaningful formula/VBA capabilities that must be preserved or deliberately replaced are summarized below.
Area | Excel/VBA behavior | Target handling
Area: Vendor; Excel/VBA behavior: CUI lookup against dated supplier sheet; Target handling: Supplier Master + normalized key + vendor status.
Area: Accounting; Excel/VBA behavior: Expense type -> main/local/subaccount mappings; Target handling: Versioned mappings in database.
Area: FX; Excel/VBA behavior: Hardcoded currency multipliers; Target handling: Effective-dated internal rates + bank settlement for card.
Area: VAT; Excel/VBA behavior: 0/5/11/21 calculations + tolerance checks; Target handling: Normalized tax breakdown + effective-dated rules.
Area: Vehicle; Excel/VBA behavior: Special 50% posting branches; Target handling: Explicit tested rule; 11 follows 21 structure.
Area: Attachments; Excel/VBA behavior: OLE embeds arbitrary local files; Target handling: Quarantine/object storage + scan + hash + line link.
Area: Approval; Excel/VBA behavior: Outlook draft / manager forward; Target handling: In-platform Approve/Reject bound to revision.
Area: ERP; Excel/VBA behavior: Macro1 populates Import and saves XLSX; Target handling: Deterministic Posting Rules Engine + values-only XLSX.

Known defects such as corrupted row references, stale 19% table metadata, stale FX metadata, first-blank-row termination, reusable Import staging, hardcoded paths and non-blocking ERP errors are explicitly NOT carried forward.
4. Current Business Process
Employee opens latest XLSM template and completes header and A-P line data.
Employee attaches supporting files into workbook, optionally prints, and drafts Outlook email.
Manager approval occurs outside Excel via email/forward/reply.
Accounting inspects workbook manually; no dedicated status/checklist exists.
Finance runs macro to transform lines into the Import staging sheet.
Import sheet is copied to XLSX and manually uploaded into ERP.
Target replacement: The future process becomes a single system of record: Employee -> Manager Approval -> Finance Review -> ERP Ready -> ERP Exported -> Posted -> Closed.

5.2 Target rules
ID | Rule | Target business rule
ID: TBR-001; Rule: Payment method; Target business rule: Every expense line/report is classified Paid personally or Company Card. Paid personally has no card reference.
ID: TBR-002; Rule: Company card; Target business rule: Company Card requires selection of an active corporate card; card owner and expense-incurred-by person are separate.
ID: TBR-003; Rule: ERP Worker; Target business rule: ERP Worker is always the person who incurred the expense.
ID: TBR-004; Rule: Report size; Target business rule: A report contains 1..50 expense lines.

ID: TBR-005; Rule: Dynamic requiredness; Target business rule: Field state is computed as REQUIRED / OPTIONAL / NOT_APPLICABLE from country, document type, expense type, payment method and policy configuration.
ID: TBR-006; Rule: Submit gate; Target business rule: Report cannot be submitted while any REQUIRED field, required evidence, or blocking validation is unresolved.
ID: TBR-007; Rule: Supplier master; Target business rule: Domestic CUI/vendor is matched to supplier master; missing ERP vendor creates Vendor Request and blocks ERP, not manager approval.

ID: TBR-008; Rule: Supplier validation; Target business rule: Normalize VAT ID/CUI; perform structural and optional external validation; external service failure must be visible and overridable by Finance with reason.
ID: TBR-009; Rule: VAT rates; Target business rule: VAT rates/mappings are effective-dated. New expenses use the rate valid on document date.
ID: TBR-010; Rule: VAT 5; Target business rule: 5% is inactive for new data entry; historical mapping may remain disabled for audit/reference.
ID: TBR-011; Rule: 0% base; Target business rule: 0% entry is base amount at 0% VAT, not VAT amount.
ID: TBR-012; Rule: VAT tolerance; Target business rule: VAT arithmetic validation uses +/-1 RON tolerance. Unresolved larger differences block ERP.
ID: TBR-013; Rule: 0% tolerance; Target business rule: 0% values within configured small tolerance (default -2..+2 RON) are ignored for VAT-code-count logic.
ID: TBR-014; Rule: Vehicle expense; Target business rule: Fuel car and Other car expenses always use 50% VAT deductibility; 11% follows the 21%-style split logic.
ID: TBR-015; Rule: Personal FX; Target business rule: Paid-personally foreign-currency expenses use effective-dated internal estimated FX rate.

ID: TBR-016; Rule: Company-card FX; Target business rule: Company-card foreign-currency ERP value uses actual bank-settled RON when reconciled; otherwise export requires Finance override/configured policy.
ID: TBR-017; Rule: Approval revision; Target business rule: Manager approval binds to a specific report revision. Employee changes after rejection create a new revision and require approval again.
ID: TBR-018; Rule: Finance edits; Target business rule: Finance may change any field after manager approval; original submitted values are retained and all changes require audit metadata.

ID: TBR-019; Rule: Material Finance change; Target business rule: Default policy: if Finance increases employee-reimbursable total after approval, manager approval is invalidated and reapproval is required; accounting-only changes or decreases do not reapprove. Configurable.
ID: TBR-020; Rule: Duplicate detection; Target business rule: Exact document hash/invoice duplicates block or require Finance resolution; fuzzy duplicates warn and require disposition.
ID: TBR-021; Rule: Card reconciliation; Target business rule: Bank statement imports create card transactions; matching supports one-to-many/many-to-one with matched amounts and audit.

ID: TBR-022; Rule: ERP readiness; Target business rule: ERP export requires manager approval, Finance review complete, vendor availability where required, valid mappings, no blocking VAT/duplicate errors, and no prior posting.
ID: TBR-023; Rule: ERP format; Target business rule: Generate values-only XLSX with worksheet name Import and exact current 24-column order.
ID: TBR-024; Rule: ERP idempotency; Target business rule: Every export has unique batch ID. A posted report cannot be exported again without authorized reopen and reason.
ID: TBR-025; Rule: Evidence; Target business rule: Each expense line may have multiple original attachments; originals are immutable and retained 5 years.
ID: TBR-026; Rule: Official package; Target business rule: Platform generates Expense Report PDF plus originals package/ZIP; PDF does not replace originals.
ID: TBR-027; Rule: Retention; Target business rule: Transactional data, evidence, approvals, exports and audit are retained 5 years from final posting/closure unless legal hold applies.
ID: TBR-028; Rule: Notifications; Target business rule: Email and in-app notifications are triggered by workflow events; email contains links/summary, not the XLSM/decont payload.
6. Employee Workflow
Employee selects New Expense Report. Header is prefilled from Employee/Organization master where possible.
Employee chooses Paid personally or Company Card. If Company Card, an active card is mandatory; card owner may differ from the person who incurred the expense.
Employee adds expenses individually. Each line supports camera/photo/PDF upload and multiple originals.
Document extraction runs asynchronously and proposes supplier, VAT ID, invoice number/date, currency, gross and VAT values.
Dynamic field rules determine required/optional/not-applicable fields. The form never asks for fields that do not apply.
Supplier, VAT, duplicate and arithmetic checks run continuously. Missing ERP vendor is visible but does not block manager submission.
Employee reviews report totals and submits. Submission creates an immutable revision and routes to the manager.
If rejected/returned, employee edits a new revision and resubmits.
6.1 Recommended employee UX
Mobile-first receipt capture with automatic rotation/compression and clear upload progress.
Autosave Draft and unsaved-change protection.
One-line expense cards on mobile; grid + drawer/editor on desktop.
Inline errors with human-readable reason and direct navigation to the affected field.
Visible states: Draft, Submitted, Manager Review, Rejected, Approved, Finance Review, Pending Vendor, Ready for ERP, ERP Exported, Posted, Closed.
7. Manager Approval Workflow

Manager approval moves entirely into the platform. The manager inbox lists amount, employee, business purpose, age and exception indicators. Review is optimized for speed: lines and evidence are visible in the same screen.
Manager opens assigned report revision.
Manager reviews line summary and originals; comments may be line-specific.
Approve records decision, actor, timestamp and exact revision hash/version.
Reject requires a reason; status returns to Employee Correction and employee receives notification.
Delegation can be configured with effective dates; organization mapping may be maintained manually or imported from an HR source.
Control: Manager approval is attached to a specific revision. It is never a free-text flag or an email artifact.
8. Accounting Workflow

Finance receives only manager-approved reports (except operational queues such as Vendor Requests). The Finance Cockpit is a purpose-built review surface rather than a second copy of the employee form.

9. ERP Export Logic

ERP remains a manual file-import integration. The web platform reproduces the validated Macro1 accounting outcomes through a deterministic server-side Posting Rules Engine. The output is a values-only .xlsx workbook with worksheet name Import and the exact 24 current columns in the same order.
9.1 ERP preflight
Approved current revision.
Finance review completed.
All required supplier/vendor accounts resolved.
No unresolved blocking VAT or duplicate errors.
GL/local/subaccount/cost-center/project mappings available.
Company-card settlement/reconciliation requirement satisfied or Finance override recorded.
Posting lines generated deterministically and validated.
Report not previously posted/exported in a conflicting lifecycle.
9.2 Export lifecycle

Each export receives an immutable ERP Batch ID, generation timestamp, rule-set version, report revision, file hash and generating user. When Finance marks the batch Posted, the report is protected from accidental reposting. Reopen requires a privileged Finance permission and mandatory reason.

10. Attachments & Reporting
10.1 Attachment model
ExpenseLine -> zero/many Attachments; report-level documents supported only for explicit report evidence.
Original bytes are immutable; SHA-256 hash, MIME/signature, original filename, size, upload actor/time and scan state are stored.
Uploads enter quarantine, are malware-scanned, then moved/marked available.
Preview derivatives and OCR output are separate from the original and may be regenerated.
Allowed types initially: PDF, JPG/JPEG, PNG, HEIC; configuration controls size/type limits.
Retention is 5 years from final posting/closure, with legal-hold capability.
10.2 Official reporting package

The official output is (1) Expense Report PDF and (2) the original documents. A one-click Evidence Package ZIP may contain Expense_Report_<ReportID>.pdf plus originals named by line/document order. The PDF summarizes employee, report, manager approval, all lines, totals, VAT, Finance review and ERP posting reference; it does not replace original evidence.

19.2 Backup and disaster recovery
PostgreSQL: continuous WAL/PITR where supported, encrypted daily backups, separate backup location, regular restore tests.
Object storage: versioning/snapshots/replication or equivalent plus encrypted backup in separate failure domain.
Configuration/IaC and master-data export kept in source-controlled deployment repository, not only on servers.
Recommended target RPO <= 15 minutes, RTO <= 4 hours; validate at least annually and after major infrastructure changes.
5-year business retention is enforced by application/storage lifecycle and is distinct from operational backup retention.

1. Viziunea produsului

Platforma trebuie sa faca procesul de deconturi sa para simplu pentru angajat si manager, dar sa ofere Finance controlul si profunzimea necesare pentru contabilitate si ERP. Complexitatea trebuie absorbita de sistem, nu expusa utilizatorului.

North Star: Un angajat trebuie sa poata fotografia/incarca documentul, verifica rapid campurile propuse si salva cheltuiala. Un manager trebuie sa poata intelege un decont si apasa Approve/Reject fara Excel. Finance trebuie sa poata face review, corectii, reconciliere si ERP dintr-un singur workbench.
1.1 Principii de experienta
Simple first: afiseaza doar informatia necesara momentului si rolului curent.
One obvious primary action per screen: New Expense Report, Submit, Approve, Complete Review, Generate ERP.
Progressive disclosure: campurile contabile avansate nu aglomereaza Employee UI.
Autosave si feedback vizibil: utilizatorul trebuie sa stie mereu daca modificarile sunt salvate.
Document-first review: receipt/invoice vizibil langa datele cheltuielii.
Status transparent: fiecare decont are un status clar, timeline si urmator pas.
No hidden logic: validarea explica de ce un camp este necesar sau de ce ERP este blocat.
Fast for frequent users: filtre, keyboard-friendly grids, bulk actions prudente si saved views pentru Finance.
Mobile-friendly pentru captura documentelor; desktop-optimized pentru Finance review.

12.1 Confirmari recomandate
Nu cere confirmare pentru Save sau editari normale; autosave reduce friction.
Cere confirmare pentru Submit, Approve, Generate ERP, Mark Posted si actiuni destructive.
Reject/Return necesita reason, nu un dialog generic Yes/No.
Dupa actiune arata feedback clar: Approved successfully, ERP file generated, Vendor resolved.
13. Limbaj vizual
Intentia este premium enterprise: calm, rapid, curat. Nu trebuie sa arate nici ca Excel, nici ca un ERP vechi.
Element | Directie
Element: Layout; Directie: Mult spatiu alb; carduri si panels doar unde ajuta ierarhia.
Element: Color; Directie: Navy/blue ca accent principal; verde succes; amber warning; rosu blocking/error; gri pentru inactive/N/A.
Element: Typography; Directie: Sans-serif moderna, foarte lizibila; ierarhie clara; valori monetare aliniate consistent.
Element: Status chips; Directie: Draft, Waiting Approval, Rejected, Finance Review, Ready for ERP, Posted etc.
Element: Tables; Directie: Header sticky, sort/filter, row hover, coloane configurabile pentru Finance.
Element: Forms; Directie: Labels permanente; help text scurt; erori sub camp; fara placeholder ca unic label.
Element: Icons; Directie: Simple, consistente; nu substituie textele pentru actiuni critice.
Element: Documents; Directie: Preview mare, controls discrete pentru zoom/rotate/page.
Premium does not mean busy: Calitatea vine din claritate, viteza, consistenta, micro-interactiuni si faptul ca sistemul face automat ce Excel-ul cerea manual - nu din animatii sau grafice decorative.

18. Error handling si controale
Field errors apar langa camp si sumar sus doar daca sunt multe.
Blocking vs Warning trebuie diferentiate clar. Warning nu trebuie sa para ca exportul este blocat daca nu este.
Job-uri asincrone (OCR, import statement, PDF) au Pending/Processing/Completed/Failed si retry controlat.
Daca upload-ul esueaza, formularul nu pierde datele deja introduse.
ERP generation este tranzactional: ori se creeaza batch complet valid, ori nu ramane output partial.
Finance edits importante cer reason; sistemul nu cere reason pentru fiecare click minor.

20. Brief pentru UX/UI designer

Design goal: Create a professional enterprise product that feels closer to modern expense platforms than to Excel/ERP. Employees and managers should need almost no training. Finance gets depth through dedicated workbench views, not by exposing technical fields everywhere.
Start with desktop designs for Employee Dashboard, Expense Line Editor, Manager Review, Finance Workbench and ERP Center.
Define mobile variants for Employee capture/edit and Manager approval.
Create a small reusable component system: page header, status chip, data table, document preview, form field, issue badge, action footer, timeline, empty state.
Test the critical journeys with Finance and 2-3 normal employees before polishing secondary screens.
Keep primary buttons persistent where long screens exist (Manager review, Finance workbench).
Design for real invoice/receipt preview and long supplier/descriptions, not demo-sized data.
Ensure all financial/error statuses work without relying only on color.

Rule ID | Rule | Target Business Rule
Rule ID: TBR-001; Rule: Payment method; Target Business Rule: Every expense line/report is classified Paid personally or Company Card. Paid personally has no card reference.
Rule ID: TBR-002; Rule: Company card; Target Business Rule: Company Card requires selection of an active corporate card; card owner and expense-incurred-by person are separate.
Rule ID: TBR-003; Rule: ERP Worker; Target Business Rule: ERP Worker is always the person who incurred the expense.
Rule ID: TBR-004; Rule: Report size; Target Business Rule: A report contains 1..50 expense lines.

Rule ID: TBR-005; Rule: Dynamic requiredness; Target Business Rule: Field state is computed as REQUIRED / OPTIONAL / NOT_APPLICABLE from country, document type, expense type, payment method and policy configuration.
Rule ID: TBR-006; Rule: Submit gate; Target Business Rule: Report cannot be submitted while any REQUIRED field, required evidence, or blocking validation is unresolved.
Rule ID: TBR-007; Rule: Supplier master; Target Business Rule: Domestic CUI/vendor is matched to supplier master; missing ERP vendor creates Vendor Request and blocks ERP, not manager approval.

Rule ID: TBR-008; Rule: Supplier validation; Target Business Rule: Normalize VAT ID/CUI; perform structural and optional external validation; external service failure must be visible and overridable by Finance with reason.
Rule ID: TBR-009; Rule: VAT rates; Target Business Rule: VAT rates/mappings are effective-dated. New expenses use the rate valid on document date.
Rule ID: TBR-010; Rule: VAT 5; Target Business Rule: 5% is inactive for new data entry; historical mapping may remain disabled for audit/reference.
Rule ID: TBR-011; Rule: 0% base; Target Business Rule: 0% entry is base amount at 0% VAT, not VAT amount.
Rule ID: TBR-012; Rule: VAT tolerance; Target Business Rule: VAT arithmetic validation uses +/-1 RON tolerance. Unresolved larger differences block ERP.
Rule ID: TBR-013; Rule: 0% tolerance; Target Business Rule: 0% values within configured small tolerance (default -2..+2 RON) are ignored for VAT-code-count logic.
Rule ID: TBR-014; Rule: Vehicle expense; Target Business Rule: Fuel car and Other car expenses always use 50% VAT deductibility; 11% follows the 21%-style split logic.
Rule ID: TBR-015; Rule: Personal FX; Target Business Rule: Paid-personally foreign-currency expenses use effective-dated internal estimated FX rate.

Rule ID: TBR-016; Rule: Company-card FX; Target Business Rule: Company-card foreign-currency ERP value uses actual bank-settled RON when reconciled; otherwise export requires Finance override/configured policy.

Rule ID: TBR-017; Rule: Approval revision; Target Business Rule: Manager approval binds to a specific report revision. Employee changes after rejection create a new revision and require approval again.
Rule ID: TBR-018; Rule: Finance edits; Target Business Rule: Finance may change any field after manager approval; original submitted values are retained and all changes require audit metadata.

Rule ID: TBR-019; Rule: Material Finance change; Target Business Rule: Default policy: if Finance increases employee-reimbursable total after approval, manager approval is invalidated and reapproval is required; accounting-only changes or decreases do not reapprove. Configurable.
Rule ID: TBR-020; Rule: Duplicate detection; Target Business Rule: Exact document hash/invoice duplicates block or require Finance resolution; fuzzy duplicates warn and require disposition.
Rule ID: TBR-021; Rule: Card reconciliation; Target Business Rule: Bank statement imports create card transactions; matching supports one-to-many/many-to-one with matched amounts and audit.

Rule ID: TBR-022; Rule: ERP readiness; Target Business Rule: ERP export requires manager approval, Finance review complete, vendor availability where required, valid mappings, no blocking VAT/duplicate errors, and no prior posting.
Rule ID: TBR-023; Rule: ERP format; Target Business Rule: Generate values-only XLSX with worksheet name Import and exact current 24-column order.
Rule ID: TBR-024; Rule: ERP idempotency; Target Business Rule: Every export has unique batch ID. A posted report cannot be exported again without authorized reopen and reason.
Rule ID: TBR-025; Rule: Evidence; Target Business Rule: Each expense line may have multiple original attachments; originals are immutable and retained 5 years.
Rule ID: TBR-026; Rule: Official package; Target Business Rule: Platform generates Expense Report PDF plus originals package/ZIP; PDF does not replace originals.
Rule ID: TBR-027; Rule: Retention; Target Business Rule: Transactional data, evidence, approvals, exports and audit are retained 5 years from final posting/closure unless legal hold applies.
Rule ID: TBR-028; Rule: Notifications; Target Business Rule: Email and in-app notifications are triggered by workflow events; email contains links/summary, not the XLSM/decont payload.
